references.title: Dynamic Sampling and Rendering of Algebraic Point Set Surfaces
Feature Preserving Point Set Surfaces based on Non-Linear Kernel Regression

filters.name: Project Vertices onto MLS Surface (APSS)
filters.shortDescription: Project a mesh or point set onto an Algebraic Point Set Surface.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Projects a mesh, or a bare point set, onto the MLS surface defined by itself or by another point set.

This is the **algebraic point set surfaces** (APSS) variant: the local approximation fitted at each point is an algebraic sphere rather than a plane, which keeps curved regions from flattening out. It needs points carrying oriented normals.

parameters.label: Point set
parameters.help: The point set (or mesh) which defines the MLS surface.

parameters.label: Proxy Mesh
parameters.help: The mesh that will be projected/resampled onto the MLS surface.

parameters.label: Selection only
parameters.help: If checked, only selected vertices will be projected.

parameters.label: MLS - Filter scale
parameters.help: Scale of the spatial low pass filter. It is relative to the radius (local point spacing) of the vertices.

parameters.label: MLS - Spherical parameter
parameters.help: Control the curvature of the fitted spheres: 0 is equivalent to a pure plane fit, 1 to a pure spherical fit, values between 0 and 1 give intermediate results, while other real values might give interesting results, but take care with extreme settings.

parameters.label: Accurate normals
parameters.help: If checked, use the accurate MLS gradient instead of the local approximation to compute the normals.

parameters.label: Refinement - Max subdivisions
parameters.help: Max number of subdivisions.

parameters.label: Refinement - Crease angle (degree)
parameters.help: Threshold angle between two faces controlling the refinement.

parameters.label: Projection - Accuracy (adv)
parameters.help: Threshold value used to stop the projections. This value is scaled by the mean point spacing to get the actual threshold.

parameters.label: Projection - Max iterations (adv)
parameters.help: Max number of iterations for the projection.

filters.name: Project Vertices onto MLS Surface (RIMLS)
filters.shortDescription: Project a mesh or point set onto a Robust Implicit MLS surface.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Projects a mesh, or a bare point set, onto the MLS surface defined by itself or by another point set.

This is the **robust implicit MLS** (RIMLS) variant: it extends implicit MLS with non-linear kernel regression, so sharp edges survive instead of being rounded away with the noise. It needs points carrying oriented normals.

parameters.label: Point set
parameters.help: The point set (or mesh) which defines the MLS surface.

parameters.label: Proxy Mesh
parameters.help: The mesh that will be projected/resampled onto the MLS surface.

parameters.label: Selection only
parameters.help: If checked, only selected vertices will be projected.

parameters.label: MLS - Filter scale
parameters.help: Scale of the spatial low pass filter. It is relative to the radius (local point spacing) of the vertices.

parameters.label: MLS - Sharpness
parameters.help: Width of the filter used by the normal refitting weight. This weight function is a Gaussian on the distance between two unit vectors: the current gradient and the input normal. Typical values range between 0.5 (sharp) and 2 (smooth).

parameters.label: MLS - Max fitting iterations
parameters.help: Max number of fitting iterations. (0 or 1 is equivalent to the standard IMLS).

parameters.label: Refinement - Max subdivisions
parameters.help: Max number of subdivisions.

parameters.label: Refinement - Crease angle (degree)
parameters.help: Threshold angle between two faces controlling the refinement.

parameters.label: Projection - Accuracy (adv)
parameters.help: Threshold value used to stop the projections. This value is scaled by the mean point spacing to get the actual threshold.

parameters.label: Projection - Max iterations (adv)
parameters.help: Max number of iterations for the projection.

filters.name: Reconstruct Surface by Marching Cubes (APSS)
filters.shortDescription: Extract an APSS iso-surface as a new mesh with marching cubes.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Extracts the iso-surface of an MLS surface as a mesh, using marching cubes. The coarse extraction is followed by an accurate projection onto the MLS surface and a zero-removal pass.

This is the **algebraic point set surfaces** (APSS) variant: the local approximation fitted at each point is an algebraic sphere rather than a plane, which keeps curved regions from flattening out. It needs points carrying oriented normals.

parameters.label: MLS - Filter scale
parameters.help: Scale of the spatial low pass filter. It is relative to the radius (local point spacing) of the vertices.

parameters.label: MLS - Spherical parameter
parameters.help: Control the curvature of the fitted spheres: 0 is equivalent to a pure plane fit, 1 to a pure spherical fit, values between 0 and 1 give intermediate results, while other real values might give interesting results, but take care with extreme settings.

parameters.label: Accurate normals
parameters.help: If checked, use the accurate MLS gradient instead of the local approximation to compute the normals.

parameters.label: Grid Resolution
parameters.help: The resolution of the grid on which we run the marching cubes. This marching cubes is memory friendly, so you can safely set large values up to 1000 or even more.

parameters.label: Projection - Accuracy (adv)
parameters.help: Threshold value used to stop the projections. This value is scaled by the mean point spacing to get the actual threshold.

parameters.label: Projection - Max iterations (adv)
parameters.help: Max number of iterations for the projection.

filters.name: Compute Curvature (APSS)
filters.shortDescription: Compute APSS curvature estimates and store them in vertex quality.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown:
Computes curvature at each vertex of a mesh or point set and stores it in the vertex scalar field. No color is baked; the view switches to scalar visualization when the filter finishes.

This is the **algebraic point set surfaces** (APSS) variant: the local approximation fitted at each point is an algebraic sphere rather than a plane, which keeps curved regions from flattening out. It needs points carrying oriented normals.

parameters.label: Selection only
parameters.help: If checked, only selected vertices will be projected.

parameters.label: Curvature type
parameters.help:
The type of the curvature to plot.
ApproxMean uses the radius of the fitted sphere as an approximation of the mean curvature.

parameters.label: MLS - Filter scale
parameters.help: Scale of the spatial low pass filter. It is relative to the radius (local point spacing) of the vertices.

parameters.label: MLS - Spherical parameter
parameters.help: Control the curvature of the fitted spheres: 0 is equivalent to a pure plane fit, 1 to a pure spherical fit, values between 0 and 1 give intermediate results, while other real values might give interesting results, but take care with extreme settings.

parameters.label: Projection - Accuracy (adv)
parameters.help: Threshold value used to stop the projections. This value is scaled by the mean point spacing to get the actual threshold.

parameters.label: Projection - Max iterations (adv)
parameters.help: Max number of iterations for the projection.

filters.name: Estimate Radius from Density
filters.shortDescription: Estimate local point spacing for each vertex.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Estimate the local point spacing (aka radius) around each vertex using a basic estimate of the local density.

parameters.label: Number of neighbors
parameters.help: Number of neighbors used to estimate the local density. Larger values lead to smoother variations.

filters.name: Select Small Disconnected Components
filters.shortDescription: Select the small disconnected components of a mesh.
filters.longDescriptionMarkdown: Select the small disconnected components of a mesh.

parameters.label: Small component ratio
parameters.help: This ratio (between 0 and 1) defines the meaning of small as the threshold ratio between the number of faces of the largest component and the other ones. A larger value will select more components.

parameters.label: Select only non closed components
parameters.help: If enabled, only non-closed connected components are selected.
